elements.element: The transition-assistance obligation is triggered on expiry or termination.

elements.evidence: Section 11.1 states that Vendor “shall provide transition assistance.”

elements.element: Transition assistance is available for up to six (6) months.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly provides assistance “for up to six (6) months.”

elements.element: Transition assistance is provided at Vendor's then-current rates.

elements.evidence: Section 11.2 states that Vendor “shall return all Customer Data.”

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within thirty (30) days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 requires return “[w]ithin thirty days after expiry, termination, or Customer's request.”

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 requires a “complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format,” including necessary relationships and metadata.

elements.element: After returning Customer Data, Vendor deletes its remaining copies.
elements.evidence: Section 11.3 requires secure deletion from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups after Customer confirms successful return, subject only to an Applicable Law retention exception.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion after the return.
elements.evidence: Section 11.3 requires an authorized officer to certify deletion in writing after Customer confirms successful return; this occurs after the return as required.

elements.element: On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly imposes this obligation on expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is available for at least ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The six-month assistance period in Section 11.1 exceeds the fallback period of 90 days.
Section 11.2 requires Vendor to return all Customer Data in an export-usable format.

elements.element: The data export occurs within thirty (30) days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 expressly sets a 30-day deadline following expiry or termination.

result.reason: The operative language implements the preferred assistance period, rates, return deadline, machine-readable format, deletion, and written certification. It also necessarily exceeds the fallback. The changes remove the contradictory immediate-discontinuation and immediate-deletion language while preserving the existing, customer-protective return and deletion mechanics. Drafting quality is reduced because “within thirty days after expiry, termination, or Customer's request” can create multiple competing deadline triggers and because certification is conditioned on Customer confirmation rather than directly triggered by completion of return.
